# Independent skeptical audit ledger

Audit begun 22 October 2026. This ledger distinguishes an analytic proof,
an exact finite reduction, a successful implementation replay, and empirical
controls. No item below is a proof of the full finite-support highway
conjecture. The sources are research notes, not externally peer-reviewed or
proof-assistant-checked mathematics.

## Model and exact global target

The complete state is the entire finite black set, current cell before its
update, and incoming heading. White means R, black means L, then flip and
move. Translating the lattice or rotating it by a quarter turn preserves the
rule; reflection alone does not preserve R/L. A periodic turn stream is not
the same statement as a translating complete board: a highway deposits an
ever-growing wake, so its full finite black set is not periodically translated.

The target is an eventual cyclic phase of the standard 104-letter word, not
merely some translating periodic word. All future-read certificates must
retain or rigorously exclude every distant initial bit and every old write.

Load-bearing implementation:

- `ant_continuation2/planar_structure/certify_exceptional_rectangle.py`
- literal candidate `exceptional_rectangle_template.json`

The candidate's two finite generator runs are not the proof. For each
parameter n, the complete field is an XOR of affine points and finite
arithmetic rays. A fixed word's repeated-cell constraints determine the
required starting color and odd-toggle set on each physical cell. On a
phase ray, every existing field component contributes an exact interval
of epochs; prior repeats contribute threshold tails. Pairwise cancellation
of all symbolic interval endpoints proves zero discrepancy for every
epoch, not just at sampled n. Infinite tails are handled with genuine
unbounded epoch intervals.

Soundness checks of the engine:

- Affine signs are accepted only when their slope and value at the lower
  parameter bound guarantee the sign for all later integers.
- Parameter-dependent ordering changes, isolated integer point/line
  collisions, and unhandled residue classes cause an assertion failure.
  This is conservative: it may reject a valid family, but cannot accept it
  by looking only at its value at the lower bound.
- Parallel and nonparallel line intersections have the correct determinant
  signs. Existing-ray bounds are clipped exactly before endpoint parity.
- Earlier copies of the current word contribute iff their positive integer
  phase offset permits an earlier epoch. Within-period repetitions are
  already included in the starting-color constraints.
- All period counts are positive throughout n >= 200. Heading reset and
  nonzero standard drift are checked for repeated words and final tails.
- Symbolic equality is only used for exact cancellation. Possible isolated
  coincidences cannot produce false accepted colors; they are either guarded
  or cause conservative refusal.

### Verifier precondition found and explicit repair

The inherited generic `word_data`/`plan` helpers do not themselves validate
the alphabet. For example, `word_data('X',0)` on a white cell accepts a
starting-color requirement while planning a left turn: `plan` treats every
non-R as L, whereas the color code treats only literal L as black. This
would be unsound if arbitrary strings were admitted as certificate words.
The mathematical API therefore needs the explicit precondition that every
word lies in {R,L}*. I checked every word string in the rectangle template,
new completion template, and original four-scatterer prefix certificate:
all 20 strings satisfy it. Thus no current claimed trajectory is invalidated.
The new completion analysis was asked to enforce the precondition at ingestion;
recovered immutable sources were not modified. Future generic reuse should
place the assertion in a hardened wrapper or in the proof-kernel API itself.

## D. Bad-window equivalence: exact scope

Pinned source:
`sources/kehao95-core/factor_language/proof/ten.md`.

For a finite initial field, finitely many forward forbidden ten-windows is
equivalent to finitely many intrinsic backward-nine-plus-current J10 events:
for t>=9 the latter is exactly the former at t-9. At most nine boundary
windows differ. Restarting after the last bad forward window leaves a finite
complete field and an all-future ten-legal stream. The source's attraction
theorem then gives standardness. Conversely an eventual standard stream has
only finitely many such bad windows.

The attraction theorem is NOT a de Bruijn graph assertion about all binary
strings. It uses physical feasibility of 150-letter words, an exhaustive
finite graph, a two-loop quotient of its nonsimple component, and an analytic
all-n,m exclusion of B A^n B A^m B. On arbitrary infinite backgrounds the
ten-legal physical eventual modes also include periods 28 and 24; their
required fresh initial-black classes rule them out on finite support.

No density-zero substitute is justified: infinitely many bad windows may
have arbitrarily small frequency. An algorithm deciding whether any future
bad window exists also does not show that the process has only finitely many.

## E. Uniform low-mass occupation bound

Source:
`first_principles_2026-10-21/ant_rethink/constructive_alternatives/explicit_low_mass_occupation_bound.md`.

The claimed bound is, for all finite seeds, all interval starts s, and N>=1,

    #{t in [s,s+N): |B_t|<=K} <= min(N, C_K N^(1-1/D_K)),
    D_0=1, D_K=2K D_(K-1)+1, C_K=2(K+1)9^K.

The finite counting proof was checked. A complete centered finite state
cannot repeat: a centered repeat gives an exact translating full-state
cycle, the endpoint mass-displacement bound forces zero drift, and the known
unboundedness theorem excludes the resulting finite-region orbit. The
heading-minus-mass invariant fixes the heading for each mass. Central
states contribute at most sum_{j<=K} binomial((2R+1)^2,j). At a noncentral
low-mass checkpoint, delete one bit at distance >R only in a comparison
orbit. Its next R observations agree except for one unit of mass. Greedy
disjoint R-blocks then give

    A_K(N) <= S_K(R)+ceil(N/R) A_(K-1)(R).

The stated rounded choice of R and constants satisfy the displayed
recurrence. This is a genuine uniform-in-seed and uniform-in-start density
bound, conditional only on the explicit separator and unboundedness inputs.
It is not pointwise divergence of mass and does not imply event finiteness.

## F. Bounded retreat and finite certificates

Sources:
`first_principles_2026-10-21/ant_rethink/constructive_alternatives/bounded_directional_retreat.md`
and `continuation_2026-10-22/ant_continuation/global_structure/retreat_area.md`.

Two independent linear forms with uniformly bounded later retreat imply
eventual translating periodicity. The future-invisibility argument correctly
waits until one form has advanced beyond the entire finite initial field.
Every earlier-written black cell that could be read later then lies in a
fixed finite window about the head. Repeated reduced complete finite states
have identical full futures by coupling, so the actual turn trace becomes
periodic up to translation. Nonzero drift follows from unboundedness.

For the stronger finite certificate, the two running frontiers must include
ALL initial black cells. This is essential, not optional. The retained
rectangle has an autonomous deterministic partial transition, and cells
newly exposed beyond a frontier are guaranteed white. A repeated allowed
state proves an infinite translating cycle without assuming future retreat.
The count 4 A 2^A gives T+1 <= 4 A(T) 2^A(T) on every nontranslating-periodic
orbit. It is a lower bound on necessary retreat, not an upper bound.

This theorem does not identify the periodic word as the standard 104-word.
The global existence of two bounded-retreat directions is also unproved.

## H. New sparse-checkpoint analytic lemmas

Source: `global_constraints.md`, Sections 2, 3, 5, and 6. Independent audit
completed 22 October 2026. These results go beyond the recovered baseline,
but do not prove the highway conjecture or eventual mass at least six.

1. **Two-sided local-core minimum:** valid. For each fixed integer time offset,
   the forward or inverse evolution depends on finitely many cells. Local
   convergence therefore makes its exact mass change equal to the checkpoint
   mass change. Integer liminf K implies eventual mass at least K. The argument
   works separately for every positive or negative offset; it does not need
   one subsequence index uniform over infinitely many offsets. The displayed
   inverse update has the correct heading signs.
2. **Favorable first southwest collider at mass at most five:** valid under
   the stated bounded-head, actual-orbit, divergent-clock hypotheses. A
   negative-sign collider with bounded x-y forces three negative and two
   positive coefficients. Remote zero charges then force an alternating
   five-edge coordinate path with two bounded endpoints. The factored
   positive-z field sum is strictly negative once the collider lies below
   both endpoint coordinates, contradicting divergent positive-z clock.
3. **Five-cell southwest exposure:** valid. Remote degree four is excluded
   before classifying the incidence graph. Cutting every anchored vertex
   leaves a q-containing strand of length 3, 4, or 5, or a four-cycle. This
   does not assume distinct anchored endpoint values: a four-edge strand may
   have t=v, and the same exponential identity applies. All remaining one-
   and two-edge components are covered, including components sharing an
   anchored vertex before cutting. In the off-center five-edge case, the
   two factorizations correctly imply r>s and v>b0 from eventual positivity
   of the full field sum; remote r consequently tends to positive infinity.
   Further subsequences may fix which of the two relevant cells supplies
   each divergent u clock. The conclusion is that both axial gaps, and the
   z gaps of every other cell from q, tend to positive infinity.
4. **Only exceptional phase 72 remains at recurrent mass five:** valid
   conditional on the invoked exact standard-word capture theorem for all
   one-black parents. The fixed parent's complete tail-entry archive is
   retained as an XOR difference from the phase-correct standard core. It
   misses the incoming trace and is fixed, hence lies outside the ordinary
   postcollision half-plane for sufficiently distant q. Exposure puts every
   other checkpoint bit outside that half-plane as well. In fact the
   z<=z(q)+58 guard alone suffices; the two axis bounds are redundant after
   exposure is established. The exceptional return can revisit the arbitrary
   fixed parent's history, so the recovered blank-parent rectangle proof
   cannot simply be reused to conclude mass-six exclusion.
5. **Uniform two-diagonal-strip bound for exceptional blank parents:** valid.
   Section 7's geometry checker proves, for every n>=200, that every read of
   the one-, two-, and three-bit parents lies in |x+y|<=82 or |x-y|<=82.
   Each point's selected normal has zero n coefficient; each periodic ray's
   selected normal has zero coefficients in both n and epoch. Parent cuts
   after segments 4 and 8 use the correct already-certified infinite tails.
   The three-bit parent is justified by the rectangle certificate's full
   no-read test for the removed northeast corner. A fresh separate replay
   passes in `audits/exceptional_diagonal_strips_replay.log`. This is an exact
   geometric consequence of the previous color certificate, not a new color
   proof from pictures or samples.
6. **Mass-five recurrence cannot have an empty local limit:** Sections 8.1-8.4
   pass audit. With all five cells escaping, only the three-plus-two strand
   and the two five-edge strand placements remain. Cells with one bounded
   and one remote coordinate miss the entire two-strip domain. In the middle
   placement, the only possible second and third collisions are the axial
   northwest and southeast cells; the complete H1/H2 bounds and ordinary
   half-plane guards force both to their exceptional coordinates. The final
   three-bit parent misses both remaining cells. The off-center orientation
   is disposed of by the one-bit parent's two upper diagonal bounds. Its
   transpose is not assumed dynamically equivalent: q,d are its only
   positive-z coefficient cells, forcing z(d)->+infinity. Once a lies on the
   northwest tail, z(a) is bounded, so s-l=z(d)-z(a)->+infinity. This correctly
   supplies the otherwise missing second-collision separation. The two-bit
   parent's z<=71 bound then excludes d. No fifth-cell interaction or
   bounded-coordinate merger has been omitted.

Consequently any hypothetical recurrent mass-five sequence has a nonempty
local limiting core, hence exactly one black cell by the earlier upper bound.
The arbitrary one-black parent's historical field remains a real obstruction;
none of these arguments establishes eventual mass at least six.

## I. Clean transverse crossing audit

Sources: `scattering/transverse/crossing.py`, `certify_crossings.py`, and
`crossings_certificate.json`. The model is explicitly an infinite XOR field:
the canonical backward-infinite incoming standard wake plus a perpendicular
bilateral settled standard wake. Sixteen specified inputs have exact future
certificates: eight same-sector cases become standard 104-word highways;
eight opposite-sector cases become RL staircases requiring infinitely many
initial black cells. This does not describe arbitrary dirty crossings.

The line/ray verifier is exact for the used drifts. Transverse intersections
solve both integer determinants; parallel intersections use direction ratio
+1 or -1. Initial field contributions, finite changes, and all preceding
same-period/earlier-period writes are XORed as epoch-interval boundaries.
No finite tail sample is used as the infinite certificate. The RL certificate
uses a four-letter period with drift (2,-2), not a two-letter period outside
the parallel-intersection routine's allowed drift ratios.

`certify_crossings.py` computes the original black field's intersection with
the entire certified future read set, including all infinite tail rays.
For each same-sector case this set is finite. Removing black cells outside
that read set leaves the entire trajectory unchanged by first-difference
coupling. The resulting complete finite kernel is independently replayed and
checked by the older finite-field tail oracle. Opposite-sector cases have
unbounded initial-black intersections and therefore no such finite kernel.
Finite seeds may nevertheless contain arbitrarily long wrong-sector rail
segments; 'not written as a clean standard wake by this ant' is not a ban on
finite input patterns or nonstandard historical fabrication.

### Exact separation and offset normalization

Independent checker: `audits/audit_crossing_normalization.py`; output:
`audits/crossing_normalization_audit.json`. The checker passes.

Let D=(-2,-2), and v be D rotated through one or three quarter turns.
The lattice generated by D and v has index eight. Its complete invariants
are x modulo 2 and x+y modulo 4, yielding representatives (a,s-a), with
a=0,1 and s=0,1,2,3. The stated offset (a,s-a-4n) differs from
(a,s-a)+nD only by an integer multiple of v, which does not change a
bilateral settled rail.

For every incoming phase i and every black settled-rail line, solving the
integer intersection equations gives a possible period epoch k=n+c. Thus
the first possible contact is the minimum of finitely many exact affine
times, not an empirical first contact extrapolated from n=20. For rotation
one, s=0,1,2,3 give constants -257,-266,-267,-360 in 104n+constant;
for rotation three they give -361,-370,-371,-464. These are independent of
a. All relevant epochs are nonnegative uniformly for n>=5.

The XOR field identity H0 XOR one period's writes = translate_D(H0) is
checked in an independent exact ray-boundary normal form. Consequently,
advancing one unperturbed period in input n+1 gives exactly the D-translate
of input n. The n=20 contact/recovery certificates therefore extend to every
integer n>=5, with time shift 104(n-20) and spatial shift (n-20)D. This is a
normalization of the stated mature clean model, not a claim that every
placement at a fixed time-zero pose is already in that model's approach
regime, nor a classification of crossings with arbitrary surrounding bits.

### Uniform finite-support transfer

The separate checker `scattering/transverse/certify_finite_transfer.py` and
its proof in `scattering/transverse/PROOF.md` now pass audit. For each of the
eight same-sector reference rails with twelve line bases b and direction v,
start with the complete thirteen-cell canonical core plus all cells
b+kD+jv, -M<=j<=M. For every integer k>=22 and M>=38, the complete finite
input has the same reference recovery and permanent standard future, shifted
by time 104k and position kD. Per-case sufficient bounds can be smaller.

The all-parameter argument has two independent guards:

- The difference D0 between the infinite incoming past and the finite core,
  after normalizing the initial standard transport, is D0+k(-D). In each
  full-drift class its support has an attained minimum m. The ordinary UNION
  of supports over all k>=K is exactly the half-ray beginning at m+K, even
  if the original support contains holes. Every finite read and infinite
  tail phase ray is tested against these half-rays. This is not XORing over
  different parameter values.
- Every prescribed read's intersection with each original static black line
  is bounded in its line index. Keeping all indices -M through M therefore
  preserves every read for all larger M. Checking each component line also
  protects sites where the two original backgrounds cancel.

The initial standard-flight prefix is justified by the canonical finite
tail certificate and exact first-contact normalization. The seed/rail union
is really disjoint for all parameters: the rail's fixed z-coordinate decreases
by 4k, while the canonical seed has a fixed larger minimum z. These facts are
now explicit executable assertions, as is coverage of exactly eight cases.
The least allowed finite input for each class is also replayed independently,
but those eight replays are controls, not the source of the quantifiers.

Fresh copies in `audits/transverse_snapshot/` pass all sixteen infinite-input
replays, all eight finite-kernel checks, and all eight uniform-transfer
checkers. Logs: `transverse_crossings_replay.log` and
`transverse_finite_transfer_replay.log`. Additional falsification controls in
`audits/audit_crossing_controls.py` pass 142,000 direct interval-membership
comparisons, an exact intersection at epoch 10^60, and rejection of an added
marker 10^60 periods ahead in every one of the sixteen proposed tails.

The writer-sector interpretation is not hiding an alternative reversed-wake
representation. The two chiral settled patterns have z-support ranges [-7,3]
and [-3,7]. Any translation equating them would have z shift -4 and one of two
x-parity representatives, (0,-4) or (1,-5); neither equates their exact black
line sets. Same-orientation translational symmetries have zero z shift and
therefore preserve the sector. This is a clean-standard-wake statement only.

## J. Finite-root token forest and standard two-spine genealogy

Sources: `causal_reduction/forest_theorem.md`, `standard_forest.md`, and
`certify_standard_forest.py`. The general finite-root forest theorem passes
audit: each deleted edge has a unique last insertion (or initial token), and
its arriving cursor node is the child of that producer. Parent times strictly
increase, and unique parentage excludes undirected cycles as well. A node
has at most four children/buds; every node ends within five physical updates.
The productive-ray equivalence correctly retains finite marked side branches
and does not claim the ray itself contains infinitely many defect marks.

The exact standard-word quotient calculation also passes audit. All visits
to any one physical cell are exhausted by solving the 104 integer equations
q_j+kD=q_i. No temporal cutoff supplies the predecessor or permanent-bud
claim. The two parent-phase cycles each have total delay 104, hence winding
one. Lifting one such cycle gives one eventual chain, not many epoch residue
classes; off-cycle phases have bounded parent distance and cannot add another
infinite end. Fixed initial history only modifies finitely many relationships
after an actual standard tail begins. Module node and bud counts correctly
allow their nodes to occur several physical periods after their spine owner.

One numerical terminology defect was found and repaired: maximum cursor-node
bush depth is six, but including terminal buds as offspring makes maximum
depth seven. Permanent bud phases 100 and 103 witness depth seven. The main
two-spine, second-child, forward-consumption, and displacement conclusions
are unaffected. Fresh replay: `audits/standard_forest_replay.log`, with a
separate checker copy and JSON in `audits/forest_snapshot/`.

None of these results says arbitrary finite seeds eventually have two
spines, bounded branches, or finite bad-window events.

## K. Exact C/V nose freshness and finite-support exclusion

Sources: `word_stabilization/cv_local_trap.py`, `verify_cv_nose.py`, and the
literal C/V footprints. The theorem passes a third independently organized
audit in `audits/audit_cv_patch.py`, with exact closure data in
`audits/cv_patch_audit.json`.

The statement is: in any physically feasible finite concatenation of C and V,
each V nose has not been read earlier in THAT concatenation. It is not a claim
that a tail's nose was unread before the tail began. The target V reads its
nose L at internal phase 13 and R at phase 17; the relevant freshness is
before the first of those reads.

The last previous read, if there were one, must be R. Its entire containing
macro is one of six exact source possibilities. After that macro, no
intermediate macro reads the nose. Tracking the forced patch colors then

## P. Autonomous coset ant: trapping, returns, and six visits per cell

The crucial separation fact is exact. For a canonical word z in S, its only
representatives in the trapped group-state region are z itself and
z R L^3 or z L R^3 when zR or zL, respectively, belongs to S. The exceptional
predecessor cell has representatives R^3,L^3. Thus an interior cell's aliases
retain its entire prefix and cannot be touched by an exterior branch. In a
module rooted at v with sign a, the predecessor cell parent(v) appears in that
branch only as v a^3, its last boundary. It cannot change earlier in the call.
The exact boundary overlaps of the two children are those used in the table.

The earliest-violation argument is not circular: before a first wrong exit
or return-ledger violation, every child return has a valid ledger. A B child
return forces immediate reentry, whose completion or escape would itself
be an earlier violation. Thus a call reaching its last boundary used only
unique G child returns. The explicit interior table both excludes a boundary
arrival after B and preserves the parent language {empty,G,B,GB}. This proves
trapping and the ledger simultaneously, even on the infinite module tree.

The refined finite interfaces also pass audit and replay. The ordinary-cell
checker expands a parent and its children, leaving four arbitrary grandchild
return ledgers. Their entry lamps are UNTRACKED; their only possible tracked
lamp is a last boundary. An unfinished grandchild cannot read that boundary,

the parent-face sign. The separate root interface gives root<=5 and special
predecessor<=3 after equal-boundary entry.

Before the first turn change there are at most four equal turns and at most

nonboundary cells are a,a^2 in the old a-root-face; their colors are opposite
that face sign. They therefore receive at most five further reads. The root
